tldr: Late-October arXiv papers pushed LLM multi-agent collaboration away from fixed workflows, toward decentralized belief-conditioned actors, goal-aware role assignment, evolving teams and calibrated confidence. The thread so far is research-only, with no shipped framework behind it.
whats_new: Two Nov 4 papers shift focus to failure and measurement: MA-Mesh adds role-based self-healing, and TandemBench benchmarks how decision models split work between agents.
why_it_matters: Research is moving from 'how agents collaborate' to 'how teams recover and how to measure coordination', the questions that decide whether multi-agent setups hold up in production.

status.detail: Academic papers only; resilience and benchmarking now join the earlier coordination-design work.

beats.headline: Goal-aware roles, evolving teams and calibrated confidence

open_questions: Does any open-source agent framework adopt role-based self-healing like MA-Mesh?
Do TandemBench results get reproduced on other multi-agent systems?
Do the dynamic-team methods report cost or latency overhead versus fixed workflows?
take_for_builders: Treat these as research signals: if you run multi-agent pipelines, test what happens when one role fails mid-task before adopting any of these methods.
